messages:
Sam (sales): Heads-up — acme.io is pushing for a mid-market package: reserved capacity (8 GPUs) + 300k burst credits for the first 6 months. They want per-token pricing details and example overage behavior. Asking for a quick recommendation.
Maya (product): @Sam can you share expected QPS / steady-state tokens/day from their sizing doc? that changes whether we recommend commit vs blended credits. :thinking:
Sam (sales): They shared a rough forecast: 350M tokens/month steady, spikes up to 1.2B tokens in big campaigns (~2x sustained). Region: us-west primarily. Security: standard SOC2, no extra compliance asks. Timeline: procurement wants a signed quote in 3 weeks.
Jordan (support): For context, they use a lot of short chat-style calls and embedding requests for search re-rank. Typical response lengths avg ~40 tokens. We saw a spike pattern: daily peaks aligned with marketing sends (10–12x baseline for an hour).
Li (finance): Quick rules of thumb: for reserved capacity discounts we need ARR commitment bands. 12-month commit at this scale should be in mid-to-high discount band. Burst credits should be priced to preserve margin — recommend shadow price ~1.5x hosted per-token rate.
Maya (product): OK — product asks: 1) what is the minimum launch scope? (pricing doc, contract language, billing flow, quota enforcement) 2) Is this a one-off commercial negotiation or should we template a "mid-market reserved+burst" SKU?
Sam (sales): They prefer a templated SKU for speed but will accept a bespoke quote if it's faster.
Maya (product): Proposal: treat this as a candidate for a template SKUs pilot if legal/finance sign off. Launch minimal acceptance criteria: a) documented per-token blended rate + burst credit price, b) billing flow handles reserved allocation + credit redemption (no manual ops), c) console shows reserved pool + consumed credits per token type, d) integration test simulating burst and auto-fallback to bursts.
Li (finance): Add: e) pricing model validated in a quick P&L calc showing >20% gross margin at expected utilization. If not, escalate to revenue ops for approval.
Jordan (support): Ops detail: we need a SLO for burst fairness and documented fallback (which model variant we route to when reserved capacity saturated). Also how quota throttles appear to customers.
Maya (product): For backlog/prioritization: recommend we create a PRD ticket with the following fields: customer profile, expected tokens/month, commit length, target discount band, required console UI changes, billing API changes, test plan, rollout checklist. Priority: P1 for this sales cycle (3-week deadline).
Sam (sales): Can product own the PRD and triage to eng? I can attach the customer email thread and use case.
Maya (product): Yes — I'll spin up the PRD. Need engineering intake: estimated engineering effort (sprint count) and whether Dedicated infra changes required for reserved pool + billing hooks. @OpsBot can you create an infra incident to estimate impact?
OpsBot: Created ticket INF-4821 assigned to eng-infra with description "reserved-pool + burst-credit billing hooks estimation". ETA for initial assessment: 3 business days.
Li (finance): I'll run an initial pricing band calc and provide two recommended quotes: templated SKU and bespoke discount path.
Jordan (support): I'll add a short test harness simulating sustained 10 RPS and burst 100 RPS for 1hr to validate quota behavior.
Maya (product): Great. Next steps: 1) PRD by EOD tomorrow, 2) Ops infra assessment in 3 days, 3) finance pricing bands in 48 hours, 4) support test harness ready in 5 days. If legal approves template language, we push template SKU; otherwise go bespoke.
Sam (sales): Thanks team — I'll sync with the customer on expectation setting. :thumbsup:
Maya (product): Prioritization note: mark this as customer-driven revenue opportunity and tag for "mid-market reserved" initiative. We'll decide template vs bespoke after inputs.
Li (finance): FYI — if we standardize this SKU we should include a clause for overage reconciliation at month-end to avoid billing disputes.
Jordan (support): +1 on reconciliation. I'll add it to the test plan.
Sam (sales): filing attached: `email_acme_proposal.pdf` (uploaded).
Maya (product): Closing loop — I'll create the PRD and link all artifacts into the ticket. Thanks everyone.
